content.text: The fetus whose presenting part is the buttocks &/or feet
Occurs in 3-5% of fetuses at term (37-40wks)
Risks of Breech Presentation: developmental dysplasia of the hip, torticollis, mild deformations
Frank: both hips are flexed & both knees are extended (the feet are adjacent to the fetal head) – MC type
Complete: both hips & both knees are flexed
Incomplete (Footling): 1 or both of the hips are not completely flexed
Physical examination – a soft mass (e.g., buttocks) instead of the normal hard surface of the skill
*Leopold maneuvers are a set of 4 maneuvers that can determine the estimated fetal weight & presenting part of the fetus
U/S can be used to confirm if diagnosis is uncertain
External cephalic version (ECV) – procedure that externally rotates fetus from a breeched position to vertex position
preferred for pt to be at least 36wks
tocolytic used to prevent uterine contractions during maneuver
